 By Joe Arruda | jarruda@courant.com | Hartford Courant PUBLISHED: November 8, 2026 at 4:59 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... STORRS – Dan Hurley will be looking for his two young centers to play well in Monday’s game against Wagner, after both Na’jai Hines and Oskar Giltay got into foul trouble and didn’t have much of an impact on the win over Michigan Friday night.
 The Seahawks’ big man standing in their way? Former Husky Youssouf Singare .
 A beloved bench player on the 2024 national championship team and part of the Huskies’ 2023 “fab five” freshman class (alongside Steph Castle, Solo Ball, Jayden Ross and Jaylin Stewart), Singare has had quite the journey since he moved to the U.S. from Bamako, Mali, back in 2019. He played in high school at Our Saviour Lutheran in The Bronx, N.Y., before appearing in 39 games over two seasons at UConn. Last year he was a reserve on the High Point team that upset Wisconsin in the first round of the NCAA Tournament, and now he’s found an opportunity to start as a 6-foot-11 true senior at Wagner.
 “He was a great soldier and a warrior here. He played a role on the ’24 team, he gave us good minutes,” Hurley said Sunday. “He’s a sweet kid, a sweet man, just a great spirit. He’s getting what he really wanted this year, a chance to get on the court and play, and he’s been productive. He’s an excellent rebounder and we obviously should have a frontcourt that’s very motivated to play well to begin with, because we’ve got a young frontcourt that’s got to improve. But yeah, Youssouf was an important part of those teams.”
 UConn center Youssouf Singare (24) and forward Samson Johnson (35) celebrate after after their win against Alabama in a NCAA college basketball game at the Final Four, Saturday, April 6, 2024, in Glendale, Ariz. (AP Photo/David J. Phillip) 
 Of course, now he is playing for the program where Hurley began his career as a college head coach back in 2010. The Seahawks won five games the year before Hurley arrived and won 13 in year one, then 25 in his second year before moving on to start another rebuild at Rhode Island.
 Monday night will be the first time Hurley’s gone against a program he’s previously coached in the regular season since he’s been at UConn. But he said that holds as much weight as the 200-win ball , which he discarded down the hallway in Hartford last week.
 “You look at how you feel about the place. Obviously we’re in the business of zero-sum competition, so I don’t think you’re very sentimental about any opponents when you play the game and you prepare for the game, because you know you’ve got a chance to really be sustainably successful when your preparation and intensity and attention to detail and urgency and execution is the same regardless of the opponent,” Hurley said. “I look at Wagner, the opportunity I got there… One of my favorite years I’ve ever had in coaching was year two there. Year One was fun, too, but it almost killed me.”
 Wagner, No. 332 in KenPom’s rankings , began its season at Boston College with a 26-point loss that served as former UConn (and Wagner) assistant Luke Murray’s first head coaching win, and then lost to 14th-ranked Miami by the same margin.
 Waterbury native Tajae Jones , a 6-foot-8 forward, is featured in the starting lineup alongside New York City guards Taj Bryant, Cam Estevez and AJ Rodriguez. Kareem Watson, another 6-8 big, has been the leading scorer off the bench with 13 points at Boston College and nine at Miami.
 For UConn, coming off of an impressive 85-77 win over No. 16 Michigan in Boston’s TD Garden on Friday, the focus will be on putting together a complete, 40-minute effort in their first game on campus at Gampel Pavilion this season.
 “Coming out of the half, I think (that) was the second time we’ve had kind of a slow start, where we didn’t take those first four minutes as seriously as we needed to and I think that’s kind of the biggest thing,” said point guard Silas Demary Jr., who was named Player of the Game, loading the stat sheet with 21 points, seven rebounds, four assists, two steals and zero turnovers. “If we can have a better start to the second half, I feel like we can have a better finish to the second half.”
 “Can’t overlook Wagner, they do a bunch of things well: push the ball in transition and run different things in half court. We’ve just got to come out and play as hard as possible,” said Braylon Mullins, who made three early 3-pointers and scored a game-high 23 points on Friday.
 The last time UConn played Wagner, also at Gampel Pavilion in the 2016-17 season-opener, Kevin Ollie’s squad was upset, 67-58.
 ‘Sensational’ freshman
 Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. described UConn freshman Colben Landrew as “sensational” after he scored 14 points and grabbed eight rebounds in just his second college game, unphased by the atmosphere and the spotlight in the sold-out NBA arena.
 “He’s not afraid of the moment,” Demary said.
 Landrew has quickly earned a role as one of the “six starters,” and when he’s in the game, it’s easy to be impressed.
 “The thing about Colben that’s one of the most important attributes is you have to be comfortable when you walk into the arena and believe that you’re gonna go out there and perform at a high level,” Hurley said. “He gets electrified when the game starts. And not every player is like that. Some players, they get nervous, they get anxiety, they get uptight, they’re not sure. He’s sure. And it’s awesome.”
 “I just want to be that spark off the bench and just keep going,” Landrew said. “Just going out there and competing. Guarding, rebounding, all the little things… Just put in the work and everything will get taken care of.”
 What to know
 Site: M&T Bank Center at Gampel Pavilion, Storrs.
 Time: 7 p.m.
 Series: UConn leads, 5-1.
 Last meeting: Nov. 11, 2016 – Wagner 67, UConn 58 at Gampel Pavilion in Storrs
 TV: TruTV – Brendan Glasheen, Jim Spanarkel, Andy Katz
 Radio:  UConn Sports Network on FOX Sports Radio 97-9 – Mike Crispino, Wayne Norman
